title: Roberts Bank Terminal 2 named project of national interest
summary: Ottawa has designated Roberts Bank Terminal 2 at the Port of Vancouver a project of national interest. The $5.9-billion expansion aims to increase container capacity by 50 per cent, and the designation is expected to accelerate it by four years.
takeaway: Port capacity is now a federal priority, so learn how project designations speed up infrastructure and shape where Canadian trade will flow.

title: Canada launches task force to digitize trade processes
summary: Transport Minister Steven MacKinnon announced the Trade Digitalization Task Force on Oct. 30. Government and industry will work together to reduce paperwork, shipping delays and administrative costs, and to improve supply chain efficiency.
takeaway: Digital trade documentation is becoming a federal priority, so comfort with customs data and trade systems will set you apart.

title: Walmart commits $6B to up distribution center automation with Symbotic
summary: Walmart is committing $6 billion to deploy Symbotic's technology at 25 regional distribution facilities. The retailer wants to improve speed and inventory replenishment.
takeaway: Warehouse automation is being funded at huge scale, so roles that combine operations knowledge with systems and process design will keep growing.

title: Manufacturing expands for 10th straight month, but Iran war weighs heavily
summary: The latest ISM Purchasing Managers' Index shows manufacturing expanded for a tenth straight month. Respondent comments grew more negative, though, citing the Iran war, prices and trade wars.
takeaway: Growth is masking buyer anxiety, so procurement teams that can manage price swings and geopolitical risk will be valued.

title: Alternative-Fuel Ship Orders Outpace Port Bunkering Infrastructure, Lloyd’s Register Warns
summary: A new Lloyd's Register report warns that the global shipping industry is ordering alternative-fuel vessels faster than ports can develop the infrastructure to fuel them. The gap highlights a mismatch between fleet orders and bunkering readiness.
takeaway: Decarbonizing freight depends on infrastructure as much as ships, so expect planning roles that weigh fuel availability against green commitments.

title: The Case For Renting The Box And Buying The Truck

title: Knight-Swift CEO says CDL crackdown could fuel lasting trucking recovery
summary: Knight-Swift CEO Adam Miller said more restrictive broker-carrier relationships could reshape competition in trucking by favoring established fleets with stronger safety and compliance records

title: U.S. changes Canadian goods facing additional 50 per cent tariff
summary: U.S. President Donald Trump is removing some Canadian wood, paper and machinery products from an additional 50 per cent tariff while extending the charge to certain valves, carpets and waste products.

title: American steel dominates Canadian imports, trade data shows
summary: Federal trade figures show American steel makes up more than half of Canada’s imports of galvanized and coated steel, complicating Cleveland-Cliffs’ argument that an influx of cheap overseas steel is one of the top causes of Stelco layoffs.
